newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah edges up, focus on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah edges up, focus on liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah edged up slightly against the dollar in early trading, with the focus seen on liquidity due to the new bank reserve requirement rate effective Wednesday.
Dealers said the rupiah was adjusted lower at the open due to the long weekend and partly due to a steady money market in the morning. The market will be closed on Friday for a public holiday.
"But we saw some uptrend in the morning. Overnight money is crawling up, thus driving the dollar a bit lower," one dealer said.
"We haven't got a clear picture yet. People are trying to test the market first," he said, adding that early injection of 3.359 trillion rupiah by the central bank helped calm operators.
But some remained worried whether the market could absorb the fall-out of the new reserve rate, which is estimated to drain between five and eight trillion rupiah from the system.
"We feel a light increase in rupiah demand. But dollar supplies seem to be enough," one Japanese bank dealer said, adding he did not detect any rush in purchase of today dollars.
Spot rupiah was at 2,407.5/08.0 at 0200 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,407.5/08.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,406.50/07.25 and 2,406.00/06.75, respectively.
Overnight money edged up to 13.0/14.0 percent from 11.0/12.0 percent and overnight swap to 0.45/0.50 from 0.3/0.4.
But a state bank dealer said he did expect any exorbitant rise in overnight money because the central bank may allow repo papers and short-term securities to steady the market.
The swap market was slow as the focus was on the money market. One-month swaps were at 11.00/11.75, two at 24.5/26.5, three at 34.50/35.25 and six at 70.00/70.75 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,401/2,593 and the conversion band to 2,401/2,449 on Tuesday.
